facts.fact: Levellers says Benin's Digital Code (Loi 2017-20, promulgated 20 April 2018, amended 2021) regulates profiling and automated individual decisions (Article 401) and requires impact assessments for high-risk automated processing, the only binding rules touching AI harms.

Levellers says the Agence des Systemes d'Information et du Numerique (ASIN) built GPT BJ, a government chatbot answering questions on the tax, digital, labour and penal codes, presented on 11 May 2023.
Levellers says Benin has no dedicated AI law, bill or statute; AI is governed indirectly through Book V of the Digital Code on personal data.

BEN.note: The only AI system named is a general-administration chatbot.

facts.fact: Levellers says the Council of Ministers adopted the National AI and Big Data Strategy 2023-2027 (SNIAM) on 18 January 2023, with four programmes, 123 actions and a projected budget of 4.68 billion CFA francs.
Levellers says operational delivery of the strategy runs through ASIN, under the finance and digital ministries, with the digital ministry leading the strategy.
Levellers says ASIN built GPT BJ, a government chatbot on Beninese legal codes, presented on 11 May 2023 at the SENIA event in Cotonou.

BEN.note: Nothing stated on the central bank.
Nothing stated on digital finance consumer protection.

facts.fact: Levellers says the APDP is an independent authority whose members are appointed by decree in the Council of Ministers, and that it licenses processing, handles complaints, investigates and imposes penalties; the 2020 amendment cut membership from eleven to eight.

BEN.note: No dated ruling or published count is stated.

facts.fact: Levellers says Book V of the Digital Code (Loi 2017-20, promulgated 20 April 2018, amended by Loi 2020-35) is Benin's data protection law and replaced the 2009 law.
Levellers says the APDP, whose members are appointed by decree, enforces Book V and imposes penalties.
Levellers says Book V of the Digital Code (Loi 2017-20, promulgated 20 April 2018) is the current data protection law.
Levellers says Benin ratified the Malabo Convention by Decret 2024-772 of 1 February 2024 and deposited its instruments on 26 November 2024.
Levellers says APDP members are appointed by decree in the Council of Ministers and the body supervises processing and imposes penalties.
Levellers says operational delivery of the AI strategy runs through ASIN, formed by merging four predecessor bodies under the finance and digital ministries, which built the GPT BJ chatbot.
Levellers says Benin ratified the Malabo Convention by Decret 2024-772 of 1 February 2024, after parliamentary authorisation on 23 January 2024, depositing its instruments on 26 November 2024.
